body_markdown:
Despite rocky financial news over the last year, Porsche is having a great time selling sports cars. While the Cayenne remains the brand’s best seller, the 911 is flying off the lots so far in 2026, and set a record with over 50,000 units sold in 2025.[Automotive News](https://www.autonews.com/volkswagen/porsche/ane-porsche-ceo-moves-to-reshape-brand-0828/) has reported that, in addition to planning an even larger SUV for the U.S. market, Porsche is also considering the return of a supercar to fill the spot in Porsche’s sports car hierarchy left void since the departure of the 918 way back in 2015.


While the decision to build a Porsche 918 successor is still being mulled over—Automotive News says the choice will be made at the end of this summer—Porsche CEO Michael Leiters seems focused on pushing Porsche to focus on sports cars. A replacement for the 918,[which has since become a hot collectible](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/hagerty-insider/sale-of-the-week/an-un-wrapped-porsche-918-nearly-doubled-in-value/) , would further help signal the brand’s identity going forward. The logical route to develop such a low-volume, high-performance car would be the same one that Audi took in developing the Nuvolari. Audi’s 1,001-hp flagship sports car, set to go into production next year, uses the Lamborghini Temerario’s twin-turbo V-8 along with a trio of electric motors. It also shares the mid-engine platform with the raging bull.


Porsche last teased a halo car in 2023 with the all-electric Mission X. A Porsche 918 successor is long overdue.


Porsche


We would expect Porsche to make the styling all its own, of course, and perhaps Stuttgart’s engineers would demand a bespoke engine for the sports car brand’s halo model. Would purists mind that the peak Porsche has such Italian roots or shares hybrid tech with Audi? Of course. But would buyers mind if the looks and performance were there? Probably not enough to matter in such a low-production offering.


An investors’ meeting planned for October 7 might be the first time any real plans for a future Porsche halo car are made public. Until then, we’ll have to imagine our fantasy 918 Spyder successor.
